newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND STRUGGLE IN DEFENCE OF WORLD SEVENS CROWN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND STRUGGLE IN DEFENCE OF WORLD SEVENS CROWN.

text.p: Holders England were warned to change their style if they are to retain the World Cup Sevens title as they struggled into the quarter-finals on Saturday.

The reigning champions now play Western Samoa for a place in the semis while Australia and New Zealand clash for a last-four berth. The other fixtures see South Africa play France and Fiji meet South Korea.
England's warning came from coach Les Cusworth after he had seen his side make heavy work of dispatching the Cook Islands 29-10 in a Pool F contest.

A member of the Barbarians side that won the Hong Kong Sevens way back in 1981, Cusworth said England must drop their 15-a-side style to compete with the Fijians, New Zealand and South Africa who, he said, were all superior in ball-handling skills and sevens' vision.
England, who earlier beat Canada 30-7, were given a nasty shock by the tiny Cook Islands in front of a capacity 40,000 crowd.

Austin Healey and Chris Sheasby had to twice bring England level in the early stages and it took further scores from that duo and Nick Beal to see them through against a country with a population of just 18,000.

"We have a lot of hard work to do - we are struggling to adjust to seven-a-side rugby after the Five Nations Championship," said Cusworth. "The most impressive teams are Fiji, New Zealand and South Africa in that order.

"Fiji have great ball handling, they support the ball carrier well and most importantly have a great understanding of the sevens game. In these wet conditions that understanding will be very important."
Fiji, yet to concede a point in the tournament, ran up 101 points with wins over Namibia 66-0 and a determined Wales side 35-0 to top the rankings for the second straight day.
Playmaker Waisale Serevi, who flourishes in the wide open spaces of seven-a-side rugby, scored two tries and six conversions as Fiji put Namibia to the sword.
"I have made a promise back home in Fiji to bring back the Melrose Cup," said Serevi, the team captain who plays his club rugby in Japan.
Meanwhile, South Africa upped their tempo from the first day and defeated Ireland 34-7 and Hong Kong 29-5.

Hong Kong, with former Australian sevens star Carl Gordon beefing up a side which already included ex-Tongan international Isi TuUivai, had earlier created a major shock by beating a strong Ireland side 26-5 but South Africa exposed their lack of pace in defence with effective kick and chase tactics.

New Zealand beat Japan 47-0 and Tonga 31-5 while veteran winger David Campese, playing his final international tournament, led Australia into the last eight with a decisive 31-19 win over Scotland who had held them to a 19-19 draw on the first day.
